name: Chemistry
notes: At least 39 credit hours in chemistry and at least 59 credit hours overall. A 2.0 GPA must be maintained in the major, excluding allied field courses.
The department also offers four focused BA tracks (biological, inorganic, organic, physical chemistry); this entry is the general BA.

CHEM 210W partially satisfies the Organic Chemistry, Upper-Level Laboratory, and Upper-Level Writing requirements at once. The app models the upper-level laboratory as ONE course; the page requires two unless CHEM 210W was completed, so if you take CHEM 208 rather than CHEM 210W you owe a second upper-level lab that the app will not prompt for.
The two organic sequences are alternatives, handled by the app's orgo-sequence equivalency group.
The upper-level courses group allows 'other science courses approved by the Undergraduate Studies Committee'; only chemistry courses are modeled. No credits may come from independent research.
STAT 180 and STAT 190 are the current numbers for the former STAT 211 and STAT 212.

requirementGroups.label: General chemistry
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: General Chemistry (4-5 credits): CHEM 131: Chemical Concepts I (or equivalent AP credit)

requirementGroups.label: Organic chemistry sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Standard Sequence: CHEM 203: Organic Chemistry I; CHEM 204: Organic Chemistry II; CHEM 207: Organic Chemistry Lab I; CHEM 208: Organic Chemistry Lab II OR CHEM 210W: Honors Organic Chemistry Lab II. Or First-Year Organic Sequence: CHEM 171; CHEM 172; CHEM 173; CHEM 210/210W

requirementGroups.label: Theory courses (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Theory (12 credits). Three of the following theory courses: CHEM 132: Chemical Concepts II; CHEM 211: Inorganic Chemistry; CHEM 251: Physical Chemistry I; CHEM 252: Physical Chemistry II

requirementGroups.label: Upper-level laboratory
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Upper-Level Laboratory (4-8 credits). One (if you have completed CHEM 210W) or two (if you have completed CHEM 208) of the following: CHEM 231W: Chemical Instrumentation; CHEM 232/232W: Molecular Spectroscopy; CHEM 234/234W: Advanced Laboratory Techniques; CHEM 244/244W: ANSEL
requirementGroups.note: Modeled as one course; a second is required if you took CHEM 208 instead of CHEM 210W.

requirementGroups.label: Upper-level chemistry courses (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Upper-Level Courses (8 credits). Complete two additional 200-level (or higher) chemistry courses or other science courses approved by the Undergraduate Studies Committee. No credits can be from independent research.

requirementGroups.label: Calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following math sequences: MATH 141, MATH 142, and MATH 143 (Calculus I, II, and III); MATH 161 and MATH 162 (Calculus IA and IIA)

requirementGroups.label: Additional mathematics, computing, or statistics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus one of the following: MATH 165: Linear Algebra With Differential Equations; MATH 163: Ordinary Differential Equations I; CSC 161: Intro to Programming; CSC 171: Intro to Computer Science; STAT 180; STAT 190; STAT 201: Introduction to Probability

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses (at least one in chemistry)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: All chemistry majors are required to complete two upper-level writing courses ('W' courses). At least one of these courses must be a chemistry department course selected from the following: CHEM 210W; CHEM 231W; CHEM 232W; CHEM 234W. Student may select another course from above or a writing course from another department to fulfill the second writing course requirement.
upperLevelWriting.note: Only one of the two must be a chemistry course; the second may be any department's W course. Modeled as two chemistry W courses so the plan is self-contained.
